skill.name: analyzing-projects
skill.description: Guides an AI assistant through structured codebase analysis to identify architecture, stack, directories, workflows, and conventions.
skill.summary: Map a project codebase into a concise architecture and workflow brief.
skill.author: CloudAI-X

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown code fences or inline code formatting, not executable Ruby backtick usage. However, the workflow asks for development commands to be verified, which can lead an assistant to run untrusted install, dev, test, or build scripts. The skill should require explicit approval and sandboxing before any project-defined command is executed.

remediation.issue: Untrusted project command verification can execute repository scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running install, dev, test, or build commands. Inspect scripts first and prefer sandboxed, read-only analysis.

remediation.issue: Read-only shell examples can hide failed file reads.
remediation.suggestion: Label ls and README checks as optional read-only commands. Report missing files instead of suppressing context that affects the analysis.

semantic_findings.title: Unscoped Project Command Verification
semantic_findings.description: The validation checklist asks users to mark development commands as verified and the output template lists install, dev, test, and build commands. In an untrusted project, running those commands can execute repository scripts without a permission or sandbox warning.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly references common project commands and asks that development commands be verified working. The risk depends on whether the assistant executes them, so confidence is high but not certain.

content.value_statement: New codebases are hard to understand without a repeatable review process. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for mapping stack, architecture, commands, and conventions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews root files and README content to build a project overview.
Identifies common language, framework, package manager, and infrastructure markers.
Maps major directories and describes their likely responsibilities.
Summarizes architecture, APIs, state, database, authentication, and testing patterns.
Produces a project report with stack, entry points, conventions, and quick commands.
limitations: It relies on available repository files and may miss behavior hidden in generated artifacts.
It cannot prove runtime behavior without optional command execution or user-provided evidence.
It does not replace a full security, dependency, or performance audit.
Command verification should require explicit user approval in untrusted projects.

use_cases.title: Onboard to a New Repository
use_cases.description: Create a concise map of stack, directories, commands, and conventions before making code changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Technical Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn repository structure and workflow clues into a readable architecture summary for maintainers.

use_cases.title: Assess Project Fit
use_cases.description: Compare technologies, testing habits, deployment markers, and organization patterns across candidate projects.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Project Overview
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this project at a high level. Identify the main purpose, stack, important directories, and the safest next files to read.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the repository structure and summarize the architecture. Include entry points, API style, data layer, authentication, and testing approach.

prompt_templates.title: Workflow and Conventions Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the development workflow and coding conventions. Report package managers, scripts, formatting tools, tests, CI markers, and contribution risks.

prompt_templates.title: Evidence-Based Technical Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce an evidence-based project analysis. Separate confirmed facts from assumptions, cite files reviewed, and flag commands that need approval before execution.

output_examples.input: Analyze an unfamiliar TypeScript web application.
output_examples.output: A concise report covering purpose, Next.js stack, source directories, API routes, database usage, test setup, and recommended first files.

output_examples.input: Explain how a backend service is organized.
output_examples.output: An architecture summary with service boundaries, entry points, configuration files, deployment markers, and workflow commands to verify with approval.

output_examples.input: Prepare onboarding notes for a mixed-language monorepo.
output_examples.output: A repository map that separates packages, shared libraries, infrastructure folders, test ownership, and areas needing maintainer clarification.

best_practices: Start with read-only inspection of README files, manifests, and directory names before deeper analysis.
Separate confirmed evidence from assumptions when describing architecture or workflows.
Ask for approval before running repository-defined commands, especially install, build, dev, or test scripts.
anti_patterns: Do not run untrusted project scripts just to complete the checklist.
Do not infer architecture from directory names when source files contradict that pattern.
Do not present generated or vendor files as the main application design.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It reviews repository files to summarize purpose, stack, architecture, directories, workflows, commands, and conventions.

faq.question: Does it execute project commands?
faq.answer: The skill includes command examples, but command execution should require explicit user approval and a safe environment.

faq.question: Can it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they can inspect repository files.

faq.question: Is it a security audit tool?
faq.answer: No. It can notice architecture and workflow risks, but it does not perform a complete security review.

faq.question: What inputs improve results?
faq.answer: A complete repository, README files, manifests, tests, CI files, and deployment configuration improve the analysis.

faq.question: How should uncertain findings be handled?
faq.answer: Unverified assumptions should be labeled as needs clarification, with the files or evidence that would resolve them.
